summary: Claude Code project template that turns a one-line game idea into a playable browser game, then helps you grow and finish it.

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: Claude Code Game Studios is a project setup for Claude Code that acts like a small game studio. You describe a game, Claude Code asks a few questions, writes a one-page brief and builds a playable browser game, then you change, grow and finish it one step at a time.
sixtySeconds.problem: Going from a game idea to something playable takes many skills. This template guides Claude Code through design, building, checking and polishing so beginners can make real games.
whoFor: Beginners who want to make a game
Claude Code users exploring game dev
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for a guided workflow with briefs, automatic checks in a headless browser, checkpoints, and a path to a real Vite and TypeScript project.

overview: Clone the repo (or use it as a template), open Claude Code in the project's root folder, and type /prototype with your idea or run /start, which asks where you are and guides you.

The first build is a browser game in prototypes/<name>/ that opens with a double-click. It is checked with scripted key presses before you get it, and the handover card says what passed and what was guessed.
Other commands include /next-step, /brainstorm, /setup-engine (for example Godot) and /cut for finishing. The project is MIT licensed.
limitations: Needs Claude Code and uses your plan's usage
Must be started from the project root
